name: Arooj Aftab
label: Verve
lede: Arooj Aftab's acoustic "Hallelujah" went around Lahore by file-sharing, and fifteen years on she was the first Pakistani artist to win a Grammy. Then she made a record about the night, and Elvis Costello played Wurlitzer on it.

eras.title: A file-shared cover and a Boston scholarship
eras.text: Aftab was born in Riyadh to Pakistani parents and raised in Lahore from age 10 or 11. She taught herself guitar and learned to sing by copying records, then reached Boston at 19 to study production and engineering. By 2010 she was in New York, editing, scoring and gigging.

years.big: "I make the music that I want to hear that I can't find anywhere."
q: I make the music that I want to hear that I can't find anywhere.
years.h: Berklee Online first, then the Boston campus at 19
years.p: Aftab began with five Berklee Online courses on a scholarship, then moved to the U.S. to study music production and engineering in person.
years.xp:
She has said the school gave her the vocabulary to talk to herself and to the wider world of music, and she graduated in 2010.

Wikipedia describes her as self-taught on guitar and in her singing style, which makes the engineering degree the one formal training that shows up on every record she makes.

years.src: Stereogum: Arooj Aftab Interview · Crack Magazine · Wikipedia: Arooj Aftab
years.h: An acoustic "Hallelujah" goes around Lahore by email
years.p: Aftab's guitar-and-voice take on Leonard Cohen's song travels on file-sharing sites and inboxes. Stereogum dates it to 2007.
years.xp: Crack describes the cover circulating by email and file-sharing, and says the response gave her the confidence to apply to Berklee. Wikipedia credits this cover and a version of "Mera Pyaar" with helping launch Pakistan's indie scene, and calls her one of the first musicians in the country to promote her work online.

years.h: Two weeks of 5 a.m. lessons with Sara Zaman in Lahore
years.p: That was the whole of Aftab's classical training, per Crack: a 2008 visit to the singer Sara Zaman's home.
years.xp: Crack says the sessions were less technical training than a lesson in connection and inspiration. Aftab built on them alone.

years.src: Wikipedia: Arooj Aftab · Stereogum: Arooj Aftab Interview
years.h: With the degree done, she takes audio jobs in New York
years.p: Aftab edits, scores films and sings around the jazz and new-music scene. Stereogum lists audio work at outlets including the Huffington Post and Vice.

years.h: NPR and WQXR put her on a list of 100 Composers Under 40
years.p: Her first national notice comes as a composer, three years before her debut album.

eras.title: A bird, then some islands
eras.text: Two records, one acoustic and one ambient and electronic, made mostly alone and mostly quiet. The press noticed, New York's new-music scene took her in, and she kept editing film on the side.

years.h: Her debut, self-released, gets four stars from the Financial Times
years.p: Bird Under Water is acoustic, in Urdu and English, with her voice out front. The review runs in March 2015.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists the release as 2014 and independent; Berklee dates it 2015, the year the reviews landed. The Financial Times four-star review is the first major-press notice on her Wikipedia page.

Aftab later told Clash the follow-up she first planned was meant to be edgier, groove-minded and more fun. A record about grief was not yet on her mind.

years.h: The New York Times files Siren Islands as classical, NPR as electronic
years.p: The ambient, electronic one came out June 12 on New Amsterdam. The Times picked "Island No. 2" among 2018's best classical tracks, and NPR listed the album among the year's best electronic music.
years.xp: That same year NPR placed her song "Lullaby" at No. 150 on its list of the 200 greatest songs by 21st-century women. Three outlets, three genre boxes.

years.h: She opens for Mitski at Brooklyn Steel
years.p: One of her biggest rooms to date is an indie-rock one.

years.h: A documentary she edited, Armed With Faith, wins an Emmy
years.p: It took the News and Documentary Emmy for outstanding politics and government documentary.

eras.title: A record for Maher
eras.text: Her younger brother Maher died in 2018, and the record she was making turned into Vulture Prince, which broke her through. Before it was out she had also recorded a trio album that would sit for years.

years.src: The Skinny · NPR: How Arooj Aftab
years.h: A trio session in Brooklyn goes on the shelf for four years
years.p: The pianist Vijay Iyer and the bassist Shahzad Ismaily join Aftab for improvised sessions that don't come out until 2023.
years.xp: The Skinny puts the recording in 2019 and the release in early 2023. NPR says it was made at Ismaily's studio in Brooklyn, and that the three describe the music as made collectively, in what they call "ritual time".

years.h: Residente's Latin Grammy winner has Aftab singing on it
years.p: She sings on "Antes Que El Mundo Se Acabe" by the Puerto Rican rapper Residente.

years.src: Wikipedia: Vulture Prince · Crack Magazine · Wikipedia: Arooj Aftab
years.h: Vulture Prince is a record for her brother Maher
years.p: Released April 23, it sets ghazals and poems around grief, with harp, violin, double bass and flugelhorn. Pitchfork gave it 8.2.
years.xp:
Aftab told Crack she had meant to follow Bird Under Water with something edgier and groove-led, even leaning toward afrobeat. After Maher's death the record's central character turned somber, a passage through which she could move her own grief.

Wikipedia credits the harpist Maeve Gilchrist, the guitarist Badi Assad and the percussionist Jamey Haddad. The Guardian ranked it No. 20 of 2021, with Laura Snapes calling Aftab the year's biggest musical revelation, and the Dutch paper de Volkskrant named it album of the year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Arooj Aftab · Stereogum: Arooj Aftab Interview · GRAMMY.com
years.h: "Mohabbat" lands on Barack Obama's summer playlist
years.p: The eight-minute song from Vulture Prince also turns up on Time and New York Times best-of-2021 rankings.
years.xp: The song went on to win the 2022 Grammy for Best Global Music Performance; Grammy.com reports it made her the first Pakistani woman to take that award.

years.h: A New Amsterdam artist signs to Verve
years.p: Wikipedia puts the deal in late 2021, after Vulture Prince: an indie new-music label's artist now on a Universal jazz label.

eras.title: The Grammy, then the trio in the open
eras.text: The win changed what rooms expected of her. She played Coachella and the Grammys, and finally released the trio record, which Pitchfork named Best New Music.

years.cap: Aftab speaking at the White House Eid reception, May 2, 2022
years.src: GRAMMY.com · Stereogum: Arooj Aftab Interview · Wikipedia: Arooj Aftab
years.h: Aftab takes Best Global Music Performance, a first for Pakistan
years.p: "Mohabbat" wins at the 64th Grammys, and she is also up for Best New Artist.
years.xp:
Grammy.com reports she is the first Pakistani woman to win the award. Stereogum notes she was the first Pakistani woman nominated by the Recording Academy in a general-field category.

Her own account of the record, from that Stereogum interview: she made a personal record she loved and did not think too much about it.

years.h: "Wait a minute, I'm from the desert," Aftab thinks at Coachella
years.p: Crack credits her as the first Pakistani artist to play the festival. Wikipedia adds Glastonbury, Primavera Sound and Roskilde to her festival dates.

years.h: President Arif Alvi gives her the Pride of Performance
years.p: It is Pakistan's top arts honor, awarded on the country's 75th independence day.

years.h: A Grammy winner goes back to Coke Studio to sing "Mehram"
years.p: Aftab joins the musician Asfar Hussain on Pakistan's biggest music franchise.

years.h: She plays the Grammys, a first for a Pakistani artist, and is nominated again
years.p: The nomination is Best Global Music Performance for "Udhero Na", with Anoushka Shankar.

years.src: Wikipedia: Love in Exile · NPR: How Arooj Aftab · Wikipedia: Arooj Aftab
years.h: Love in Exile runs 75 minutes, and Pitchfork calls it Best New Music
years.p: Released March 24 on Verve: voice, piano, electric bass and Moog from Aftab, Iyer and Ismaily. Pitchfork gave it 8.5.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports a Metacritic score of 85, five stars each from the Guardian and Mojo, and a No. 10 finish on the New York Times' year-end list, with Pitchfork placing it No. 25 of 2023. The trio has said they share responsibility for the music, which is what they credit for their freedom as individuals.

At the 66th Grammys the album was nominated for Best Alternative Jazz Album and "Shadow Forces" for Best Global Music Performance.

yt: Aftab, Iyer and Ismaily at Tiny Desk
years.h: NPR's Tiny Desk gets the trio, and "Eyes of the Endless"
years.p: Aftab sings, Iyer plays Fender Rhodes and piano, Ismaily plays bass and Moog, all in the moment, as NPR describes it.

eras.title: She makes a record about the night
eras.text: Aftab wrote Night Reign on the road after two years of shows, in a better mood than Vulture Prince found her. Tessa Thompson directed the first video, and the guest list ran to Elvis Costello and Moor Mother.

years.h: Tessa Thompson makes her directing debut on "Raat Ki Rani"
years.p: The first single and its video arrive April 18, with the album announcement.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls the video Thompson's directorial debut. The second single, "Whiskey", followed on May 7.

years.cap: Aftab at the Roundhouse, London, November 2024
years.src: Wikipedia: Night Reign · Album of the Year: Night Reign · The FADER
years.h: Night Reign has Elvis Costello on Wurlitzer
years.p: Released May 31 on Verve, 48 minutes of Pakistani folk and bebop in Urdu and English. Pitchfork's Andy Cush gave it 8.3 and called it a "wondrous fourth album".
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits Vijay Iyer on piano, Kaki King on guitar and Maeve Gilchrist on harp, with Costello on Wurlitzer and the poet Moor Mother on vocals. The FADER adds Gyan Riley on guitar, Darian Donovan Thomas on violin, Petros Klampanis on bass, Cautious Clay and Marc Anthony Thompson.

Aftab told the FADER that Moor Mother "can articulate a thing like a knife covered in honey." Per Album of the Year, Pitchfork's 83 sat in a critic average of 86; Metacritic aggregated 89.

The FADER reports "Na Gul" and "Saaqi" are the first musical settings of the 18th-century Urdu poet Mah Laqa Bai Chanda, whose work Aftab spent seven or eight years going back to. "Bolo Na" was written in high school and shelved as too cheesy.

q: The night became a great friend.
years.src: The Quietus · The FADER · Crack Magazine
years.h: The road is where Night Reign gets written
years.p: The FADER counts more than 200 shows behind her when she wrote it. She told The Quietus the shows, the jet lag and the flights all happen at night.
years.xp: Crack had already noted that she performs in darkness with silhouetted staging, so the title was less a pivot than a confession. Of the move on from Vulture Prince, she told The Quietus: "This album is not a place to park your sadness. Move on with me."

years.cap: Aftab at TivoliVredenburg, Utrecht, Le Guess Who?
years.h: She curates Le Guess Who? in Utrecht, and books her father
years.p: Her picks for the November 7 to 10 festival include Meshell Ndegeocello, Aja Monet, Dina El Wedidi, Noura Mint Seymali, Zsela and her own father.

years.src: Album of the Year: Pitchfork's 50 Best Albums of 2024
years.h: Pitchfork's 50 Best Albums of 2024 has Night Reign at No. 17
years.p: That is seven places outside the top ten.

eras.title: Two more nominations, and a duet with Beck
eras.text: Night Reign went back to the Grammys, and a War Child compilation put Aftab on a song with Beck.

years.h: Night Reign is up for two Grammys
years.p: Best Alternative Jazz Album for the record, and Best Global Music Performance for "Raat Ki Rani", at the 67th ceremony.

years.cap: Aftab at the opening night of Fear of 13 on Broadway, April 15, 2026
years.h: Beck and Aftab cover "Lilac Wine" for War Child
years.p: The duet is on the Help(2) compilation, which raises money for War Child's work.
